query: evidence that older methods for For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send through stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and mark every other candidate deferred by publishing its source index on the pose diagnostics together with that pair's RGB and depth capture stamps. The handling process can then tell which pallets in the still-changing scene were detected but not posed. have been superseded
findings: Scene-cloud registration that returns one pallet pose and names no other pallet is the older method. Shao, Fan, Zhu, Lu, and Lang, Sensors 2023, 23(3):1217, say existing pose methods miss real-time accuracy because the scene cloud is enormous. They pass-through filter, voxel-downsample, plane-segment a single target cloud, and register it with AGWF-FPFH, SAC-IA, and ICP. Against FPFH and SHOT, that change is a faster descriptor on the same registration: more than 30% off feature-extraction time and more than 35% accuracy. Lourenco, Arsenio, Garrote, and Nunes, ICINCO 2024, are the later detector-then-crop pipeline. YOLOv8 runs first, and for each detection that contains a pallet they crop that box's RGB and depth so the pose net sees one object at a time. That later pipeline still sends every pallet detection through stage 2. Those other pallets are posed. They are not left as a deferred source index with that pair's RGB and depth stamps.

A 6D pose for every detected pallet is still current, so that full pass has not been superseded. Wu and Demeester, VISIGRAPP 2026, pass the detector bounding boxes into FoundationPose, and the pose selection module writes a 6D pose for each pallet bin. Their second-stage choice ranks rotation hypotheses of that bin. Meng, Ren, Yu, Yin, Wang, and Men, Sensors 2024, 24(16):5330, say most earlier research positioned a single pallet and ignored stacks. They still compute centers, then keep one target by a width-pixel window (WP and WT), a depth window (D-DF to D+DB), and unloading priority, with the upper pallet first, and they transform that one target into the forklift frame. Lang2Lift, Nguyen et al., arXiv:2508.15427, outputs one top-1 mask per prompt and runs FoundationPose on that mask. Jeevanandam et al., IROS 2025, say a 6DoF estimator can pose every object in a stack, and obstructed poses are unsuitable for grasping, so their selection sits after those poses exist.

Throwing away every detection below a score threshold, and keeping no identity for it, is the older bookkeeping that has been superseded when the scene is still changing. Zhang et al., ByteTrack, ECCV 2022, say trackers that keep only boxes above a threshold throw away true objects and fragment trajectories. BYTE keeps almost every box, splits a high-score set from a low-score set, and associates the low-score set with tracks the first pass left unmatched. Unmatched low-score boxes are still deleted as background. ByteTrack does not publish a per-frame source index with that pair's RGB stamp and depth stamp. vision_msgs Detection2D.id is an optional id meant to stay the same across messages, and it may be empty. It is not the index of this pair's detection list.

Pairing the two images by arrival, or stamping the pair with one clock reading, is the older sync. sensor_msgs/Image says the header stamp should be the acquisition time of that image. message_filters ApproximateTime matches on those header stamps. Its allow_headerless path, which fills a missing stamp with current ROS time, is to be avoided because the delay is unpredictable. Detection2D says the source pixels are not in the message: the detection header should match the source header, and the consumer recovers that source with an exact or approximate synchronizer. An approximate pair can carry two different acquisition stamps, so one header cannot name both captures. The deferred diagnostic has to publish the source index with that pair's RGB stamp and depth stamp. Meng's other pallets are already in the same view, and Lang2Lift's pick is in a cluttered outdoor scene, so a later frame is not a stand-in for the detections this pair already saw.
